Backend/IaC release: the 3 Function Apps, portal (frontend + backend), and
Bicep/deploy scripts. Cloud Imaging Client and Media Builder ship from their own
release streams (tags `mse-ci-client-v*` / `mse-ci-mediabuilder-v*`).

### New role: Operator

This release adds the `CloudImaging.Operator` user role: OS, boot and recovery images,
Locations, Wi-Fi networks, Autopilot decisions and every report, without Branding, Configuration
or the boot media certificate. Existing roles and access are unchanged until someone is assigned
the new role.

**Administrators of existing tenants**: add `CloudImaging.Operator` to the **Cloud Imaging
Portal** and **Cloud Imaging Media Builder** app registrations, assign it, and have assigned users
sign out and back in. Do not change, remove or re-create any existing role or assignment. Follow
[Add the Operator role](https://github.com/MSEndpointMgr/CloudImaging/blob/main/docs/upgrade-instructions.md#add-the-operator-role)
in the upgrade instructions, and upgrade Media Builder to `mse-ci-mediabuilder-v1.1.0` as well.

Reports session data (`GET /api/session-history`) now refuses Technician tokens called directly.
The Portal never showed Reports to Technicians, and their Dashboard is unchanged.

### Setup profiles

A new **Imaging** > **Setup Profiles** page: registry values, PowerShell scripts and an optional
answer file applied to devices before Windows starts, targeted by the location on the USB media.
Scripts run **Offline**, in the boot image right after the image is applied, or during
**Specialize**, in Windows setup before OOBE. The deployment timeline gains an optional **Prepare
setup** step that shows what was written and run. Every save is a version that can be viewed and
restored.

- **Scripts per location**: each script runs at all of the profile's locations or only at the ones
  you choose, and a device downloads and runs only its own. The scripts card has a location filter
  that shows exactly what a device from a location runs, and the run order is changed by typing a
  number or dragging a row.
- **Limits**: up to 1000 scripts of up to 24 MB each and a 2 MB answer file per profile, with no
  total limit. Each script and answer file is uploaded on its own when its dialog's Done is
  pressed, with progress and Retry, and opens in the editor whatever its size.

- **Roles**: Operators and Administrators create, edit, duplicate, delete and restore profiles,
  scripts and answer files included. Technicians view them read-only. Administrators set how many
  versions are kept (**Configuration** > **Miscellaneous**, default 25).
- **Infrastructure**: redeploy the Template Spec to add the `setup-profiles` blob container.
  Imaging Core creates its new tables itself. No data migration.
- **Upgrade order**: backend, then Media Builder `mse-ci-mediabuilder-v1.1.0`, then new boot
  images with Client `mse-ci-client-v1.1.0` on updated USB media. Devices on older boot images
  image without their profile, and the timeline shows Prepare setup as Not run. Follow
  [Turn on setup profiles](https://github.com/MSEndpointMgr/CloudImaging/blob/main/docs/upgrade-instructions.md#turn-on-setup-profiles).

See [Setup profiles](https://github.com/MSEndpointMgr/CloudImaging/blob/main/docs/setup-profiles.md).

### Signed boot image update checks

Every boot image contains the boot media private key, so the Device Gateway now hands out a boot
image download link only to media that proves it holds that key: the update check is signed and
each signature can be used once. The unsigned check that earlier Clients send is no longer
answered.

**Regenerate boot images.** USB media built with a Client before `mse-ci-client-v1.1.0` stops
updating itself as soon as the backend is upgraded; it keeps working for imaging. Generate new boot
images with Client `mse-ci-client-v1.1.0` and prepare the USB media again. Follow
[Regenerate boot images for signed update checks](https://github.com/MSEndpointMgr/CloudImaging/blob/main/docs/upgrade-instructions.md#regenerate-boot-images-for-signed-update-checks).

### Boot media certificate rotation without re-preparing every drive

**Rotate** now asks how long the Device Gateway keeps accepting the certificate it replaces:
**Stop immediately**, 7, 14 (default) or 30 days. During that overlap existing USB media keeps
working and updates itself to a new boot image built with the new certificate, Wi-Fi file
included, so drives only need preparing again if they do not boot online in time. The
Certificates tab shows the previous certificate and when it stops being accepted, and **Stop
accepting…** ends the overlap at once, for example when a certificate is compromised. Generate is
only offered while no certificate exists. See
[Rotating the Boot Media Certificate](https://github.com/MSEndpointMgr/CloudImaging/blob/main/docs/operations-runbook.md#rotating-the-boot-media-certificate).

### Device Gateway and hosting hardening

- The Device Gateway rejects a client certificate whose extended key usage does not include
  client authentication.
- Calls that carry no session token (session start, boot image update check, Wi-Fi networks,
  Autopilot) are limited to 300 per minute per client address, well above what a site's devices
  send in normal use.
- All four App Services require HTTPS and TLS 1.2 or later, including the deployment endpoint,
  and FTP is turned off. The three Function Apps also turn off basic authentication for
  deployment, which they never use. The portal backend keeps it for `install.ps1` and
  `upgrade.ps1`. `upgrade.ps1` applies these settings on every run, so no extra step is needed.
